readings.title: Wisdom's Public Proclamation
readings.subtitle: Wisdom cries out in the streets, offering her invaluable treasures.
readings.text: [Proverbs 8:1] Does not wisdom call, And understanding lift up her voice? [2] On the top of the heights along the way, Between the paths she has taken her stand. [3] Beside the gates, leading to the city, At the entrances, she shouts: [4] “<dq>O men, <dn>I</dn> call, to you, And <dn>my</dn> voice is to the sons of men.</dq> [5] <dq>“You simple ones, understand insight, And you fools, be of an understanding heart.</dq> [6] <dq>“Listen, for <dn>I</dn> speak noble words, And the opening of <dn>my</dn> lips is about straightness;</dq> [7] <dq>“For <dn>my</dn> mouth speaks truth; And wrongness is an abomination to <dn>my</dn> lips.</dq> [8] <dq>“All the words of <dn>my</dn> mouth are in righteousness, None of them twisted or crooked,</dq> [9] <dq>“All of them plain to him who understands, And straight to those who find knowledge.</dq> [10] <dq>“Accept <dn>my</dn> discipline, and not silver, And knowledge rather than choice gold;</dq> [11] <dq>“For wisdom is better than rubies, And all delights are not comparable to her.”</dq>

readings.title: The Nature and Rewards of Wisdom
readings.subtitle: Wisdom describes her virtues and the enduring wealth she bestows.
readings.text: [12] <dq>“<dn>I</dn>, wisdom, have dwelt with insight, And <dn>I</dn> find knowledge, foresight.</dq> [13] <dq>“The fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is to hate <dn>את</dn> evil. <dn>I</dn> have hated <dn>את</dn> pride and arrogance, And the evil way, And the perverse mouth.</dq> [14] <dq>

readings.title: The Nature and Rewards of Wisdom
readings.subtitle: Wisdom describes her virtues and the enduring wealth she bestows.
readings.text: [12] <dq>“<dn>I</dn>, wisdom, have dwelt with insight, And <dn>I</dn> find knowledge, foresight.</dq> [13] <dq>“The fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is to hate <dn>את</dn> evil. <dn>I</dn> have hated <dn>את</dn> pride and arrogance, And the evil way, And the perverse mouth.</dq> [14] <dq>"Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom; <dn>I</dn> am understanding, mightiness is mine.</dq> [15] <dq>“By me sovereigns reign, And rulers make righteous inscriptions.</dq> [16] <dq>“By me princes rule, and nobles, All the judges of the earth.</dq> [17] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> love <dn>את</dn> those who love me, And those who earnestly seek me do find me.</dq> [18] <dq>“Riches and esteem are with me, Enduring wealth and righteousness.</dq> [19] <dq>“<dn>My</dn> fruit is better than gold and fine gold, And <dn>my</dn> increase than choice silver.</dq> [20] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> walk in the way of righteousness, In the midst of the paths of right-ruling,</dq> [21] <dq>“To bestow <dn>את</dn> substance on those who love me, And to fill <dn>את</dn> their treasuries.”</dq>

readings.title: Wisdom at Creation
readings.subtitle: Wisdom recounts her existence with YeHoVaH before the world began.
readings.text: [22] <dq>“<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> possessed <dn>את</dn> me, The beginning of <dn>His</dn> way, As the first of <dn>His</dn> works of old.</dq> [23] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> was set up ages ago, at the first, Before the earth ever was.</dq> [24] <dq>“When there were no depths <dn>I</dn> was brought forth, When there were no springs heavy with water.</dq> [25] <dq>“Before mountains were sunk, Before the hills, <dn>I</dn> was brought forth,</dq> [26] <dq>“Before <dn>He</dn> had made the earth and the fields, Or the first dust of the world.</dq> [27] <dq>“When <dn>He</dn> prepared the heavens, <dn>I</dn> was there, When <dn>He</dn> inscribed a circle on the face of the deep,</dq> [28] <dq>“When <dn>He</dn> set the clouds above, When <dn>He</dn> made the fountains of the deep strong,</dq> [29] <dq>“When <dn>He</dn> gave to the sea its law, So that the waters would not transgress <dn>His</dn> mouth, When <dn>He</dn> inscribed the foundations of the earth,</dq> [30] <dq>“Then <dn>I</dn> was beside <dn>Him</dn>, a master workman, And <dn>I</dn> was <dn>His</dn> delight, day by day Rejoicing before <dn>Him</dn> all the time,</dq> [31] <dq>“Rejoicing in the world, <dn>His</dn> earth; And <dn>my</dn> delights were with the sons of men.”</dq>

readings.title: The Path to Life
readings.subtitle: A final plea to heed discipline and find life, or to choose death by hating wisdom.
readings.text: [32] <dq>“And now, listen to me, you children, For blessed are they who guard <dn>my</dn> ways.</dq> [33] <dq>“Listen to discipline and become wise, And do not refuse it.</dq> [34] <dq>“Blessed is the man who listens to me, Watching daily at <dn>my</dn> gates, Waiting at the posts of <dn>my</dn> doors.</dq> [35] <dq>“For whoever finds me shall find life, And obtain favour from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,</dq> [36] <dq>“But he who sins against me injures <dn>את</dn> himself; All who hate me love death!”</dq>

readings.title: Wisdom's House and Banquet
readings.subtitle: Wisdom builds her house and invites the simple to her table to find understanding and life.
readings.text: [Proverbs 9:1] Wisdom has built her house, She has hewn out its seven columns, [2] She has slaughtered her meat, She has mixed her wine, She has also prepared her table. [3] She has sent out her young women, She cries out from the highest places of the city: [4] “<dq>Who is simple? Let him turn in here!</dq>” As for him who lacks heart, she says to him, [5] <dq>"Come, eat of <dn>my</dn> bread and drink of the wine <dn>I</dn> have mixed.”</dq> [6] <dq>Leave the simple ones and live, And walk in the way of understanding.</dq>

readings.title: The Beginning of Wisdom
readings.subtitle: The fear of YeHoVaH is the foundation of wisdom, and each person bears the consequence of their choice.
readings.text: [7] He who reproves a scoffer gets <dn>את</dn> shame for himself, And he who rebukes a wrong one gets himself a blemish. [8] Do not reprove a scoffer, lest he hate you; Reprove a wise one, and he loves you. [9] Give instruction to a wise one, and he is wiser still; Teach a righteous one, and he increases in learning. [10] The fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is the beginning of wisdom, And the knowledge of the Set-apart One is understanding. [11] For by me your days become many, And years of life are added to you. [12] If you have become wise, You have become wise for yourself, And if you have scoffed, You alone bear it.

readings.title: Folly's Deceptive Call
readings.subtitle: The foolish woman offers stolen pleasures that lead to the depths of She'ol.
readings.text: [13] A foolish woman is loud, Simple, and without knowledge. [14] For she has seated herself At the door of her house, On a seat by the highest places of the city, [15] To call to those who pass by, Who go straight on their way: [16] “Who is simple? Let him turn in here.” And as for him who lacks heart, she says to him, [17] “Stolen waters are sweet, And bread eaten in secret is pleasant.” [18] But he does not know that the dead are there, Her guests are in the depths of She’ol.

readings.title: Contrasts of the Righteous and the Wicked
readings.subtitle: A series of couplets contrasting the outcomes of wisdom and folly, diligence and laziness.
readings.text: [Proverbs 10:1] Proverbs of Shelomoh: A wise son makes a father rejoice, But a foolish son is his mother’s sorrow. [2] Treasures of wrongness are of no value, But righteousness delivers from <dn>את</dn> death. [3] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does not let the being of the righteous go hungry, But <dn>He</dn> thrusts away <dn>את</dn> the desire of the wrong. [4] Poor is he who works with a lazy hand, But the hand of the hard worker makes rich. [5] He who gathers in summer is a wise son, He who sleeps in harvest is a son who causes shame. [6] Blessings are on the head of the righteous, But violence covers the mouth of the wrong. [7] The remembrance of the righteous is blessed, But the name of the wrong ones rot. [8] The wise in heart accepts <dn>את</dn> commands, But one with foolish lips falls. [9] He who walks in integrity walks safely, But he who perverts his ways becomes known. [10] He who winks with the eye causes sorrow, And one with foolish lips falls. [11] The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, But violence covers the mouth of the wrong.

readings.title: The Power of the Tongue
readings.subtitle: Proverbs concerning hatred and love, the value of wise speech, and the danger of many words.
readings.text: [12] Hatred stirs up strife, But love covers <dn>את</dn> all transgressions. [13] Wisdom is found on the lips of him who has understanding, But a rod is for the back of him who lacks heart. [14] The wise treasure up knowledge, But the mouth of a fool is near ruin. [15] The rich man’s wealth is his strong city; The ruin of the poor is their poverty. [16] The wage of the righteous is for life, The increase of the wrong is for sin. [17] He who heeds discipline is in the way of life, But he who refuses reproof goes astray. [18] He who hides hatred has lying lips, And he who sends out a slander is a fool. [19] When words are many, Transgression is not absent, But he who restrains his lips is wise. [20] The tongue of the righteous is choice silver; The heart of the wrong is of little value. [21] The lips of the righteous shepherd many, But fools die for lack of heart.

readings.title: The Security of the Godly
readings.subtitle: The blessing of YeHoVaH brings wealth without sorrow, and the righteous have an everlasting foundation.
readings.text: [22] The blessing of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> makes one rich, And <dn>He</dn> adds no pain with it. [23] To work out wicked schemes Is like sport to a fool, But wisdom is for a man of understanding. [24] What the wrong one fears comes upon him, But the desire of the righteous is granted. [25] As the whirlwind passes by, The wrong one is no more, But the righteous has an everlasting foundation. [26] As vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, So is the lazy one to those who send him. [27] The fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> prolongs days, But the years of the wrong ones are shortened. [28] The righteous look forward to joy, But the expectancy of the wrong ones perish. [29] The way of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is a stronghold for the perfect, But ruin to the workers of wickedness. [30] The righteous is never shaken, While the wrong shall not dwell in the earth. [31] The mouth of the righteous brings forth <dn>את</dn> wisdom, But the tongue of perverseness is cut out. [32] The lips of the righteous know what is pleasing, But the mouth of the wrong speaks perverseness.
